verdict.rationale: BigQuery's pricing docs set out two compute models: on-demand per TiB scanned with the first 1 TiB free each month, and capacity-based slots billed over time. A free tier (10 GiB storage, 1 TiB queries) and custom daily quotas help bound spend, and community users confirm that dry runs show bytes to be scanned before a query runs. However, one hands-on report describes a $14,000 surprise bill, and another user says cost is hidden behind 'TBs scanned' and 'slots', so a monthly estimate requires translating your workload into those units. Missing for 10: concrete published rates for storage and slots in the evidence, a documented pricing calculator or monthly-estimation workflow, and a direct cost-in-dollars display before committing.
